25 An electromagnetic wave in free space has a frequency of 2.5  1014
Hz.
Which region of the electromagnetic spectrum includes this frequency?
A
infrared
B
microwave
C
ultraviolet
D
X-ray

hints: Notice the given value $2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ and recall that red visible light is about $4 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ - is the given frequency just above or just below visible?
Remember the order of frequency in the spectrum: microwave and infrared are lower frequency than visible, while ultraviolet and X-ray are higher frequency than visible.
Check with $c = f\lambda$ using $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ to find the wavelength in metres and compare it with the $700 \text{ nm}$ red end of visible light.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: an electromagnetic wave in free space with $f = 2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$.
Recall that all electromagnetic waves in free space travel at $c = 3.0 \times 10^{8} \text{ m s}^{-1}$ and that $c = f\lambda$.

Compare with visible light: red light has $\lambda$ about $7 \times 10^{-7} \text{ m}$ and $f$ about $4.3 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so this wave has longer wavelength and lower frequency than visible light.
Longer wavelength than red light and lower frequency than visible light places the wave in the infrared region. This is option A

A.explanation: Frequency $2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ is just below visible light and gives $\lambda$ about $1.2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ m}$, which is in the infrared range.

B.explanation: Microwave frequencies are much lower, typically $10^{9}$ to $10^{12} \text{ Hz}$, so $2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ is far too high.

C.explanation: Ultraviolet has higher frequency than visible light, above about $8 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$, so $2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ is too low.

D.explanation: X-ray frequencies are far higher, typically $10^{16}$ to $10^{19} \text{ Hz}$, so $2.5 \times 10^{14} \text{ Hz}$ is far too low.
